headline_marked: Meta launches [[Meta One]] subscription with expanded AI tools
headline: Meta launches Meta One subscription with expanded AI tools
summary: New plans offer enhanced AI features like image and video generation, alongside premium access to Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp.
details: Meta has introduced Meta One, a new subscription service designed to monetize its AI models and provide users with expanded AI capabilities across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp. This move follows Meta's significant investment in AI technologies and the introduction of tiered subscriptions for its social apps.

The Meta One service includes two main plans for individual users: Core at $7.99/month and Premium at $19.99/month. Both plans bundle existing features from Facebook Plus, Instagram Plus, and WhatsApp Plus, with the primary differentiator being increased access to AI tools.

Subscribers can leverage AI-powered features such as Muse Image and Muse Video for generating pictures and videos, utilize the AI-powered Restyle feature for editing Instagram Stories, and access voice effects and creative tools more frequently. The Premium plan offers greater usage limits for these AI functionalities compared to the Core plan.

For businesses and creators, Meta offers a range of plans including Essential ($14.99/month+), Advanced ($49.99/month+), Expert ($149/month+), and Max ($499/month+). These tiers provide tools for presence management, expanded access to the Meta Business Agent, verified badges, and advanced features like story scheduling and exportable analytics.

The business-focused plans introduce enhanced profiles, a bold 'follow' button on reels, and automated follow invitations. Meta intends to further develop these plans with features for end-to-end marketing, business operations, and content optimization, including an upcoming Edits Plus plan for its content-creation app.

These new subscription offerings are projected to significantly boost Meta's revenue. BNP Paribas forecasts an additional $13.5 billion by 2028, while Truist estimates Meta could generate $20 billion by 2030 from its subscription strategy.

headline_marked: Asus [[RTX 5090 bundle]] is cheapest way to buy flagship GPU
headline: Asus RTX 5090 bundle is cheapest way to buy flagship GPU
summary: A $10,850 Asus ROG Edition 20 bundle is the cheapest way to get Nvidia's flagship RTX 5090 GPU, which is otherwise nearly impossible to find.
details: Asus is offering a limited-edition ROG Edition 20 anniversary bundle for $10,849.96, which includes an RTX 5090 graphics card, a high-end motherboard, a 3000W PSU, and an open-frame PC case.
While the bundle's price is astronomical, it's currently the most affordable way to acquire an RTX 5090, with individual cards scarce and scalped at prices nearing $10,000.
The bundle features the ROG Astral RTX 5090 Edition 20, boasting an upgraded design with an 800W power connector, a glass backplate, an OLED screen, and faster clock speeds.
Other components include the ROG Crosshair X870E Edition 20 motherboard with support for nine M.2 SSDs, the ROG Thor Titanium III 3000W PSU, and the ROG GR20 open-frame EATX PC case.
The RTX 5090 remains the most powerful consumer GPU available, featuring 21,760 CUDA cores, 22GB of GDDR7 VRAM, and up to 1,792 GB/s bandwidth, making it ideal for demanding gaming and AI tasks.
caption:
Nvidia's RTX 5090 GPU is virtually unobtainable, but Asus' $10,850 anniversary bundle is now the cheapest way to get one.

Asus is offering a limited-edition ROG Edition 20 anniversary bundle for $10,849.96, which includes an RTX 5090 graphics card, a high-end motherboard, a 3000W PSU, and an open-frame PC case.

While the bundle's price is astronomical, it's currently the most affordable way to acquire an RTX 5090, with individual cards scarce and scalped at prices nearing $10,000.

The bundle features the ROG Astral RTX 5090 Edition 20, boasting an upgraded design with an 800W power connector, a glass backplate, an OLED screen, and faster clock speeds.

Other components include the ROG Crosshair X870E Edition 20 motherboard with support for nine M.2 SSDs, the ROG Thor Titanium III 3000W PSU, and the ROG GR20 open-frame EATX PC case.

The RTX 5090 remains the most powerful consumer GPU available, featuring 21,760 CUDA cores, 22GB of GDDR7 VRAM, and up to 1,792 GB/s bandwidth, making it ideal for demanding gaming and AI tasks.
